meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'kind', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'morning', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: я, пожалуй, пойду = I think I'll be going

examples.trans: All right, I think I'll be going.

examples.text: Ладно, я, пожалуй, пойду. Пока, Нина!
examples.trans: All right, I think I'll go. Bye, Nina!

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'why'.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ставка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'exhibition' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A representative of the exhibition from Milan called.

examples.text: Почему, Вик, на выставку не улетели?
examples.trans: Why didn't you fly out to the exhibition?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

улететь.gloss: to fly away, to depart by plane

meanings.en: to fly away, to fly out, to depart by air
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'лететь'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to fly away', forming an aspectual pair with 'улетать'.

examples.trans: What do you mean you didn't fly out?
Our plane has already flown out.

examples.text: Да, Аллочка? Как ты не улетела? Почему?
examples.trans: Yes, Allochka? What do you mean you didn't fly out? Why?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('like that, so') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'менить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to cancel', paired with 'отменять'.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

звонить.gloss: to call, to phone; to ring

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to call', forming an aspectual pair with 'позвонить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to ring') (a bell or phone) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: declines like какой: какая-то, какое-то, какие-то

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'entrepreneur', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.text: Вам же звонил там какой-то предприниматель.
Вам же утром звонил какой-то знакомый предприниматель.
examples.trans: Some entrepreneur you know called you in the morning, right?

examples.text: Богатый предприниматель заказал весь наш зал для делового ужина.
examples.trans: A wealthy entrepreneur booked our entire hall for a business dinner.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('what') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'меняться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be canceled', forming an aspectual pair with 'отмениться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: С этого момента вся правда отменяется!
examples.trans: From this moment on, all truth is canceled!

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Relational Russian adjective in '-ский' meaning 'Moscow', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Паша, слушай. Это были не местные, а московские.
examples.trans: Pasha, listen. They weren't local police, they were from Moscow.

meanings.note: International compound from Greek 'tele' (far) + 'phone' (voice, sound).

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('here') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('! = you'll see!') (emphasis) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'number; phone number; hotel room' in everyday Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('phone number') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('hotel room') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Don't laugh. Read me the number.

набирать.gloss: to gain, gather, recruit; to dial

meanings.note: набирать популярность = to gain popularity

meanings.en: to dial (a phone number); to recruit
meanings.note: Secondary conversational sense ('to dial (a phone number); to recruit') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The firm is recruiting new employees.

examples.text: Он теперь набирает популярность. И Осипенко может проиграть выборы.
examples.trans: He is now gaining popularity. And Osipenko might lose the election.

meanings.note: with a past-tense verb: я бы подумал = I would think
wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to fire', forming an aspectual pair with 'увольнять'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to fly', forming an aspectual pair with 'полететь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to race, to speed along') (figuratively) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Все видели, как ты из окна летел.
examples.trans: Everyone saw you fly out the window.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Declinable masculine noun meaning 'account', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('bill, check') (in a restaurant) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Или счёт в банке. Потому что они все обманщики.
examples.trans: Or a bank account. Because they are all cheats.
